macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks suffer sharp AI-led selloff
items.summary: The Dow fell 3.4% to 51,523, the S&P 500 dropped 4.4% to 7,353.73, and the Nasdaq plunged 5.5% to 24,315. Semiconductor shares led the decline as investors worried that political and regulatory changes could slow data-center investment.[2][10]

items.title: Chip stocks tumble across markets
items.summary: Nvidia fell 9.3%, Broadcom 11%, AMD 17.3%, and Qualcomm 9.5% after disappointing guidance, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 12.3%. The selloff spread to Asian markets on Friday.[2][5][10]

items.title: Fed hike expectations ease but officials remain hawkish
items.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said policy should move into restrictive territory, while Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin emphasized inflation risks. Futures pricing put the probability of a December rate increase near 70%, down from roughly 83% previously.[4][10]

items.title: U.S. economic data shows resilient labor conditions
items.summary: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 for the week ending October 31, while third-quarter productivity increased at a 3.6% annualized rate and unit labor costs declined 0.7%. Markets largely overlooked the stronger data amid the equity selloff.[4][10]

items.title: Treasury yields fall as investors seek safety
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield declined to about 4.84% from 4.89%, while the 30-year yield slipped to 5.26%. The move reflected safe-haven demand during the sharp equity-market decline.[2][3]

items.title: Bank of England raises interest rates
items.summary: The Bank of England unanimously increased interest rates by 25 basis points, adding to the global focus on persistent inflation and restrictive monetary policy.[2]

items.title: Global equity funds record seventh consecutive week of inflows
items.summary: Global equity funds attracted inflows through November 4 even as U.S. and Asian markets weakened. Steady central-bank rates and lower crude prices supported investor allocations, while concerns about AI infrastructure costs remained a risk.[1]

items.title: Bosch reports strong quarterly profit growth
items.summary: Bosch’s Indian unit reported a nearly 22% year-over-year increase in second-quarter profit, driven by stronger demand for components used in passenger cars and commercial vehicles.[1]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum fall sharply amid broad market sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to roughly $75,558, down 5.32% over 24 hours, while Ethereum fell to about $2,236, down 7.23%. The declines came alongside a major sell-off in U.S. equities and approximately $370 million in leveraged crypto liquidations.[1][4]

items.title: House Democrats consider broader crypto market-structure bill
items.summary: House Democrats are reportedly discussing a new crypto market-structure bill that would expand SEC oversight, narrow the CFTC’s role, and incorporate provisions from earlier proposals. The discussions follow the stalled CLARITY Act in the Senate.[1][2]

items.title: Hong Kong passes crypto-asset reporting legislation
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Legislative Council passed legislation implementing the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework. Automatic exchange of crypto-tax information is expected to begin in 2028.[1]

items.title: Binance hack investigation details $6.34 billion attack attempt
items.summary: Binance’s preliminary investigation said attackers used fake job interviews, malware and internal AI tools to infiltrate wallet infrastructure. About $2.85 billion in digital assets was reportedly frozen or intercepted.[1]

items.title: Solana leads blockchain ecosystems in reported DEX activity
items.summary: Solana reportedly processed more than Ethereum and its layer-2 networks combined in 24-hour decentralized-exchange volume, while its ecosystem revenue also exceeded that of Ethereum and BNB in the cited data.[3]

items.title: Fartcoin surpasses $1 billion market capitalization
items.summary: Fartcoin reportedly exceeded a $1 billion market cap and overtook Bonk as the leading Solana-based meme coin by market capitalization, with approximately 148,000 holders.[3]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber for advanced vulnerability research
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized cybersecurity model designed to find and exploit software vulnerabilities within authorized testing environments. The model is initially available to selected customers in the Daybreak Red program and reportedly identified more than 81 previously unknown Firefox vulnerabilities.

items.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash video model
items.summary: Google rolled out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, which can generate video clips of up to 15 seconds, improves reference adherence and supports conversational editing. Google also reduced pricing by 30% compared with the previous version.

items.title: METR reports acceleration in Anthropic model development
items.summary: AI research nonprofit METR reported that Anthropic’s models are improving on well-specified tasks at roughly twice the pace observed between March 2024 and October 2025. The report attributed about 80% of the acceleration to Anthropic’s internal use of AI systems.

items.title: UK announces additional AI safety and biosecurity funding
items.summary: The UK government announced an additional £120 million for the UK AI Security Institute and AI biosecurity initiatives as part of a new artificial-intelligence funding package.

items.title: Meta expands Muse with voice mode and expressive avatars
items.summary: Meta began rolling out voice conversations and expressive animated avatars in its Muse application in the United States, giving users more interactive ways to communicate with its AI agent.

items.title: Mercedes-Benz deploys on-device conversational AI
items.summary: Mercedes-Benz announced a partnership with MIT spinout Liquid AI to run conversational AI models directly in vehicles rather than relying exclusively on cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small
items.summary: Thinking Machines introduced Inkling 2 Small through its Tinker platform for fine-tuning and inference. The model’s weights were initially kept closed.

items.title: Deep Principle releases open-weight scientific model
items.summary: Deep Principle released Hydrogen-1.0, an open-weight model aimed at chemistry, materials science and life-sciences applications.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA owners reportedly discuss acquiring Unity
items.summary: Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, which acquired Electronic Arts this year, are reportedly in early talks to buy Unity. Unity reported $622.1 million in quarterly revenue and its first profit since going public in 2020, but no deal has been agreed.[4][10]

items.title: Steam tightens game-submission requirements amid AI-game influx
items.summary: Valve has updated Steam’s submission process after developers reported delays linked to a surge of low-effort generative-AI games. New checks include running builds through Steam for at least five minutes and verifying common redistributables and supported features.[2]

items.title: Bilibili Gaming reaches League of Legends Worlds semifinals
items.summary: Bilibili Gaming defeated Dplus KIA 3–0 in the 2026 World Championship quarterfinals to advance to the semifinals.[3]

items.title: Rainbow Six Siege BLAST Major Osaka begins
items.summary: The final Rainbow Six Siege Major of the 2026 season has started in Osaka, with 20 teams competing for a $600,000 prize pool.[3]

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo released its Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the platform’s major 2026 releases.[3][5]

items.title: Rockstar publishes new GTA 6 screenshots ahead of launch
items.summary: Rockstar released 39 additional Grand Theft Auto VI screenshots two weeks before the game’s scheduled November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.[3]

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla receives major free update
items.summary: Ubisoft released a free update adding New Game Plus, new content, and progression changes to Assassin’s Creed Valhalla on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.[3]

items.title: God of War Laufey reportedly delayed to May 2027
items.summary: Santa Monica Studio has reportedly moved the PlayStation 5 exclusive God of War Laufey from February 16 to May 20, 2027.[3]

items.title: Game companies expand accessibility labeling
items.summary: Several major game companies have begun using accessibility tags covering 24 features, including clear subtitles, narrated menus, and button remapping, through the Accessible Games Initiative.[9]

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero reportedly sells four million copies
items.summary: Phantom Blade Zero reportedly reached four million copies sold in three days, alongside strong player numbers on Steam.[1]

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California over child-safety law
items.summary: The companies filed separate lawsuits challenging a California law that would restrict addictive social-media features, including endless scrolling and autoplay, for users under 16. The law is scheduled to take effect in January 2027.

items.title: U.S. semiconductor industry expands training programs amid labor concerns
items.summary: Community colleges are launching accelerated semiconductor-training programs to help fill a projected shortage of engineers and technicians in the U.S. chip industry by 2030.

items.title: Motorola launches Signature 27 smartphone
items.summary: Motorola introduced the Signature 27, a premium smartphone priced from $1,599 and featuring a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor, a 6.8-inch Tandem OLED display and seven years of operating-system updates.

items.title: Mercedes-Benz introduces on-device conversational software for vehicles
items.summary: Mercedes-Benz is rolling out conversational models that run directly on its vehicles rather than relying on cloud processing, through a partnership with Liquid AI.

items.title: France reports cyberattack attempt targeting blood banks
items.summary: French authorities said attackers attempted to manipulate blood-bank refrigerator temperatures but were stopped before any damage occurred. The incident highlights continuing vulnerabilities in connected critical infrastructure.

items.title: European supermarkets investigate remote attacks on refrigeration systems
items.summary: Supermarkets in Sweden, Belgium and Italy reported that refrigeration units were remotely taken over, causing spoiled food and prompting officials to investigate the attacks.
